about: What Animundo is missing, most wanted first in each list. tools/catalogue.py turns this and the game's data into docs/catalogue.md. When something is added, its row shows as done; then delete it here. status: wanted, in_progress (say who), check (something to decide first) or later.

animals.name: Bank vole
animals.feeds: Fox (its main food all year), kestrel (its main food), owls later
animals.needs: New model. Tags `small_mammal`, `vole`; the kestrel then `hunts: ["vole"]`. Code: wild prey that isn't a rabbit (`prey.gd` only makes rabbits), and a kestrel that hovers and drops onto prey.

animals.name: Mountain hare
animals.feeds: Fox, later lynx and eagle owl
animals.needs: New model from a spec, with a white `winter` coat. It replaces the "rabbit": European rabbits don't live wild in Nuuksio (ART.md: real species only).

animals.name: Young perch and young roach
animals.feeds: Perch (its main food from summer on: perch eat small fish, even young perch), pike
animals.needs: No new model: the perch and roach models at baby size, from the baby stage (decision 0010). Tag `fry`; the perch then `hunts: ["fry"]`. Code: hunters only catch prey much smaller than themselves, and the player's fish can chase fish.

animals.name: Common frog
animals.needs: New model. Code: an animal that lives on land and in water (a new archetype).

animals.name: Common lizard
animals.needs: New model. Cold-blooded, basks on sunny rocks.

animals.name: Chaffinch, with eggs and nestlings
animals.feeds: Fox (spring: birds and eggs), later sparrowhawk
animals.needs: New model. Tag `small_bird`. Code: nests with eggs and young.

animals.name: Night animals: bats and owls
animals.needs: Code first: how night works has to be tested before the first night animal (decision 0014, open). See docs/animals-wanted.md.

plants.name: Wild raspberry
plants.feeds: Fox, squirrel (`berries`: players are already told they ate wild raspberries)
plants.needs: Data only. Clearings, forest edges, old fields. About 1–1.5 m of upright canes, `kind: "bush"`. White flowers in June, red berries July–August.

plants.name: Crowberry
plants.feeds: Fox, squirrel (`berries`: players are already told they ate crowberries), later birds
plants.needs: Data only. Rocky hilltops and pine heath with heather (`on: ["grass", "rock"]`). A low evergreen mat; black berries from August that stay into winter.

plants.name: Red clover and white clover
plants.feeds: Hare (`clover`: players are already told they ate clover), bumblebee
plants.needs: Data only for the look: meadows, roadsides, around old farms, not inside the forest. Two specs, one per species. Code to be the bee's flowers (see core team work).

plants.name: Wild carrot: check first
plants.needs: Rare in Finland, only a few places on the south coast, so it probably shouldn't be in Nuuksio. Decide with the core team whether to replace the `carrot` food with plants hares really eat there (grasses, herbs, willow twigs).

plants.name: Goat willow (as a shrub)
plants.feeds: Bumblebee (catkins are its first food, April–May), hare (twigs and bark in winter)
plants.needs: Data only for the shrub: forest edges, clearings, lake shores. Code: bee food from a plant, and winter browse for hares.

plants.name: Wavy hair-grass
plants.needs: Data only, `kind: "ground"`. The commonest grass of dry forest floor. Could replace the generic grass tuft inside the forest.

plants.name: Chanterelle
plants.needs: Data only, `kind: "ground"`. Mossy spruce and mixed forest, July–September.

plants.name: Fireweed
plants.needs: Data only. Clearings, burnt and open ground, roadsides. Up to 1.5 m: pink spikes July–August, red leaves and white seed fluff in autumn.

plants.name: Wood anemone
plants.needs: Data only, `kind: "ground"`. Leafy groves and herb-rich spruce forest. White flowers in early May, gone by midsummer.

plants.name: Reindeer lichen
plants.needs: Data only, `kind: "ground"`, `on: ["rock"]`. Pale grey-green mats on rocky pine hilltops, the same all year.

plants.name: Red-stemmed feathermoss
plants.feeds: Nest lining for squirrels and birds
plants.needs: Data only, `kind: "ground"`. Green carpets under spruce, nearly everywhere.

plants.name: Juniper
plants.needs: Data only, `kind: "bush"`. Rocky pine heath and dry slopes. Evergreen; berry-cones take two years to ripen from green to blue-black.

plants.name: Bracken
plants.needs: Data only, `kind: "bush"`. Spruce and mixed forest. Fronds unroll in late May, turn brown in autumn and die back in winter; long `leaf` shapes make the fronds.

plants.name: Lily of the valley
plants.needs: Data only, `kind: "ground"`. Dry leafy groves and forest edges. White bells in June, poisonous red berries in autumn. Finland's national flower.

plants.name: Peat moss
plants.needs: Code first: bog ground in the terrain.

plants.name: Cloudberry
plants.needs: Code first: bog ground. Orange berries in July.

plants.name: Labrador tea
plants.needs: Code first: bog ground. White flowers in June.

plants.name: Hare's-tail cottongrass
plants.needs: Code first: bog ground. White fluffy heads in late May and June.

trees.name: Aspen, grey alder, goat willow as trees
trees.needs: Code: trees are still made in code. Trees as data recipes are undecided (decision 0013): measure first.

foods.name: Spruce cones and seeds
foods.feeds: Squirrel (its main food autumn to spring)

foods.name: Mushrooms
foods.feeds: Squirrel (summer and autumn; it dries them on branches)
foods.needs: Code: a new food kind that uses the mushroom plants.

foods.name: Water plants
foods.feeds: Moose (summer: it wades in and eats pondweed and water lilies), roach
foods.needs: Code: the lake's pondweed and lilies become food.

foods.name: Grass and herbs
foods.needs: Code: a new food kind, grazing the meadow's grass tufts. Today a hare only finds clover and wild carrot.

foods.name: Worms, snails and larvae in the mud
foods.feeds: Bream (its main food: it sucks them from the bottom), roach
foods.needs: Code: a new food kind on the lake bottom, found by digging in the mud. Today bottom feeders eat the water insects drifting in open water.

foods.name: Beetles for the fox
foods.needs: Data only: add `insects` to the fox's `diet`. Its field guide already says it eats insects.

foods.name: Ducklings
foods.needs: New model and a duck family on the lake. Tag `small_bird`.

core.name: Remake the code-made ground cover as specs
core.why: Grass tufts, stones, the four flowers (oxeye daisy, heather, harebell, tormentil), reeds, water lilies and pondweed then follow the same rules, art guide and seasons. The bee's flowers are tied to the bee's code, so they move last.

core.name: Bee flowers from plant specs
core.why: A plant part (bilberry flowers, clover, willow catkins, heather spikes) counts as a flower a bee can drink from while it's shown. Bilberry flowers and willow catkins are the bumblebee's real spring food.

core.name: Food on real plants
core.why: A berry food spot uses the plant model (a bilberry with berries) instead of a box, and only has berries while the plant does.

core.name: Bog ground in the terrain
core.why: Nuuksio has small bogs; bog plants need somewhere to grow.

core.name: Swimming land animals
core.why: A generated `swim` clip for every four-legged animal (dog paddle: short fast leg strokes, head up, tail trailing), played while it's in water, with a preview tile. Foxes, squirrels and hares really swim, but in the game they play their walk animation, so they look like they're walking on the lake bottom.

core.name: Body-plan templates
core.why: A starting spec per body plan (four-legged, bird, fish), so agents and contributors copy the closest one instead of starting from scratch.

core.name: Swimming birds
core.why: Ducks and grebes floating on the surface. No swimming birds yet.

core.name: Trees as recipes
core.why: So contributors can add tree species without code (decision 0013). Undecided: measure first.

core.name: Curled-up sleep
core.why: Animals now lie down on their bellies with the legs folded under them, dropped to their real hip height (or `sleep_drop` and `sleep_legs` in the spec). Some animals sleep curled up instead: a fox with its tail over its nose, a squirrel wrapped in its tail. That needs a curl pose for the body and tail chain.

core.name: Stride and eating reach per animal
core.why: Walk, run and eat use fixed angles. Long legs get huge strides (the moose needed `swing` 0.75), and a tall animal can't lower its head to the ground. Let a spec set stride length and how low or high it eats (a grazing hare, a browsing moose).

core.name: Build report: body and separate parts
core.why: The build prints one triangle total. Separate parts (antlers, fins, spots, eyes) share the budget, and the body never gets fewer than 200, so the budget can be silently exceeded or the body starved. Print the body and the separate parts separately, and warn at the minimum.

core.name: Bird wings: fold and flap
core.why: The default fold tips the wing out instead of down (roll is applied before yaw), folded wings stay as wide as spread ones, and the flap is a symmetric ±52° around the rest pose. Apply the tip-down tilt after the sweep, narrow folded wings, and make the downstroke shorter than the upstroke.

core.name: Insect wingbeat that sweeps
core.why: The bee's buzz flips the wings up and down every frame. Real insect wings sweep forward and back; up and down reads as a jittery V.

core.name: Fish poses
core.why: Fish use only idle and swim. The generated eat and sleep clips tip a fish over. A hovering idle, a slight head yaw against the tail while swimming, and resting near the bottom would suit fish better.
